sections.section_title: The Third Sign -- Seven Angels with Seven Last Plagues
sections.summary: The neutral reading introduces the seven angels carrying the seven last plagues in which God's wrath is completed; the section is a narrative introduction to the bowl judgments rather than a statement about the believer's standing.

The neutral reading presents those who were victorious over the beast, his image, and the number of his name, standing on the sea of glass mixed with fire, holding harps of God and singing the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb.
sections.relevance: The conquerors are identified by a threefold overcoming corresponding to the threefold coercion of chapter 13: they conquered 'from the beast' (political worship), 'from his image' (idolatrous worship), and 'from the number of his name' (economic mark). The neutral reading explicitly addresses the paradox: 'In 13:7, the beast was given to make war with the saints and to overcome them. Yet the same people the beast overcame are now described as those who were victorious over the beast.' The resolution is that 'the faithful conquer by refusing to yield, even at the cost of their lives.' The victory is present-participial (nikōntas), indicating an abiding identity defined by their conquering. This implies that the overcomers' standing was determined by their maintained refusal to capitulate, not by an irrevocable status.
key_phrases: those who were victorious over the beast and his image and the number of his name
Great and marvelous are Your works
Righteous and true are Your ways

sections.section_title: The Heavenly Temple Opens and the Angels Emerge
sections.summary: The neutral reading describes the opening of the heavenly temple, the emergence of the seven priestly angels with bowls of wrath, and the filling of the temple with smoke from God's glory; the section is a preparation scene for the bowl judgments rather than a statement about the believer's standing.
